content.title: Three Keys  a Pick No 3 seed Illinois vs No 9 seed Iowa
content.text: Illini Inquirer's Kyle Tausk previews Illinois' Elite Eight matchup against No. 9 seed Iowa on Saturday.No. 3 seed Illinois (27-8) vs. No. 9 seed Iowa (24-12)Date & Time: March 28, 5:09 p.m. CTLocation: Toyota Center (Houston, Texas)TV: TBS/TruTV (Kevin Harlan, Robbie Hummel, Stan Van Gundy & Lauren Shehadi)QUICK HITSIllinois is looking to reach the program's sixth all-time Final Four, third since the tournament expanded in 1975 and first since 2005.The Illini are coming off a 65-55 win over No. 2 seed Houston in the Sweet Sixteen on Thursday, advancing to the program's second Elite Eight in three seasons.Illinois is fourth on KenPom, currently ranking second nationally in adjusted offensive efficiency and 21st nationally in adjusted defensive efficiency.The Illini are making their 11th all-time Elite Eight appearance and sixth since the tournament expanded to 32 teams in 1975.Illinois has a 49-36 all-time record in NCAA Tournament games. Its 49 wins rank tied for 18th among all schools and second among schools yet to win a national championship, only trailing Purdue.The Illini are 9-4 in the NCAA Tournament as a No. 3 seed. They are 36-16 all-time in the NCAA Tournament as the higher (better) seed.Brad Underwood is 9-5 in the NCAA Tournament during his Illinois tenure and 11-9 in his career, having led Illinois to the Elite Eight twice during his tenure.Illinois is 95-77 all-time against Iowa. The Illini beat the Hawkeyes, 75-69, in Iowa City on Jan. 11.Ben McCollum is in his first season as head coach at Iowa and is making his first Elite Eight appearance. He led Drake to a 31-4 record and a Round of 32 appearance in the NCAA Tournament last season after previously winning four Division II national championships at Northwest Missouri State. McCollum is 39-8 in single-elimination tournament games during his head coaching career.The Hawkeyes defeated No. 4 seed Nebraska, 77-71, on Thursday in the Sweet Sixteen after upsetting No. 1 seed Florida in the Round of 32 and beating No. 8 seed Clemson in the Round of 64.Iowa is currently 22nd on KenPom, ranking 20th nationally in adjusted offensive efficiency and 32nd nationally in adjusted defensive efficiency.The Hawkeyes finished in ninth place in the Big Ten with a 10-10 conference record and are the lowest-seeded team still alive in the NCAA Tournament. They went 0-6 against KenPom top-10 opponents during the regular season.Illinois is a 6.5-point favorite in this matchup, which has an over/under of 137.5. LoginNever a doubt for David Mirkovic in decision to return to Illini: 'There was no other option'Mirkovic announced on Wednesday that he will return for his sophomore season.GORDYVILLE — For 25 minutes, David Mirkovic held virtual court on Twitch. He bounced around topics from his favorite NFL team to Buzz Lightyear to his college major. It was every bit of a filibuster, but endearing in a way only Mirkovic seems capable.Then he got to the heart of the matter. Mirkovic thanked the some 3,000 fans watching live at 2 p.m. on a Wednesday — he's a man by the people, for the people, after all — for a stellar season with the Illinois basketball team that ended in a run to the Final Four. Mirkovic, the cowboy hat-wearing manchild, has become a fan favorite around these central Illinois parts. Just as Mirkovic was about to make his decision about a return to Illinois for a sophomore year or a departure, presumably to the NBA, a screensaver took over his live Twitch feed for several seconds before a Michael Jordan-like "I'm back" announcement made it official that the 6-foot-9, 250-pound forward is returning to his sophomore season.Mirkovic returned on camera after a minute or so in his orange No. 0 jersey with his now-somewhat-famous cowboy hat on, flanked by student managers for the basketball program."I knew I was going to come back," Mirkovic said at the annual Kickin' Cancer dinner at Gordyville USA. "There was no other option. After the last game, I told my agent immediately that I was going to be back and there was no question about it."Though the announcement came Wednesday, Mirkovic said the return was "officially, officially" known about a week ago and that those close to him knew he was returning to the program for a second season. With All-American guard Keaton Wagler heading to the NBA, Mirkovic returns as the face of the Illini and one of the biggest personalities in college basketball Unofficially? Mirkovic — who earned Big Ten All-Freshman honors after averaging 13.3 points, 8.0 rebounds and 2.6 assists last season — has known for months that he planned to return to Illinois. Heck, he knew when he stepped on campus late last summer that his only other basketball home would be in the NBA.
